title: Nadella Takes Stand in Musk vs. OpenAI Trial, Denies Microsoft Meddling
excerpt: Microsoft CEO testifies he never heard objections from Musk during $13 billion OpenAI investment, weakening lawsuit claims
body:
**A High-Stakes Courtroom Showdown**

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella took the witness stand in Oakland on Monday in the blockbuster Elon Musk vs. OpenAI trial, delivering testimony that could reshape the outcome of one of Silicon Valley's most consequential legal battles. Musk's lawsuit alleges OpenAI betrayed its nonprofit mission after receiving $38 million in donations, transforming into an $850 billion for-profit juggernaut under Microsoft's influence.

Nadella struck directly at the heart of Musk's claims. He testified that Musk never raised objections during Microsoft's $13 billion investment in OpenAI and characterized the partnership as purely commercial. He also revealed Microsoft absorbed a $15 million loss on its Azure cloud platform from the deal — hardly the predatory arrangement Musk's legal team has portrayed.

**Sutskever Adds a Twist**

OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever also testified, admitting he once contemplated removing CEO Sam Altman over concerns about candor, though he later signed a petition to reinstate him. Sutskever has separately alleged a "consistent pattern of lying" by Altman — testimony that adds complexity even as it does not directly help Musk's case.

Musk is seeking $150 billion in damages. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers is expected to follow jury rulings on liability. Sam Altman is scheduled to testify later this week, with the verdict likely to set precedent for how AI companies structure nonprofit-to-profit transitions.
nri_angle: Nadella, one of the most prominent Indian-American tech leaders, is at the center of a trial that could redefine AI governance and corporate accountability in Silicon Valley.
